review_candidates.title: Global MEL Senior Associate (Fixed-Term)
review_candidates.description: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. About The Role We are looking for a strong analyst to provide technical guidance, analytical support, and quality assurance across a portfolio of 2–3 country programs within One Acre Fund’s growth country portfolio. Countries of operation currently include Tanzania, DRC, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Uganda, Zambia, and Burundi. Country MEL Leads are responsible for day-to-day MEL operations in their respective programs. The Global MEL Senior Associate complements this by bringing dedicated technical depth and cross-country perspective reviewing and strengthening analytical approaches, advising on evaluation methodology, building tools and frameworks that leads can adopt, and surfacing learnings across the portfolio. Over time, this role is expected to meaningfully build MEL capacity in the countries it supports. Beyond country support, the role contributes to selected Global MEL initiatives such as the design and rollout of team trainings, development of shared tools and templates, and cross-program methodology work. Depending on candidate's profile, the portfolio may also include analytical support for One Acre Fund’s Agroforestry program, a large and technically complex area with significant opportunity for rigorous measurement work. The Global MEL Senior Associate will report to a Senior Manager on the Global MEL Team. Responsibilities Country Portfolio Support Serve as the primary technical resource for country MEL Leads in your assigned portfolio, providing structured guidance, review, and feedback throughout the program cycle. Review and strengthen survey instruments and data collection approaches, including questionnaire design and programming in CommCare (or equivalent), prior to deployment. Assess and improve data quality backcheck processes, identifying opportunities to automate checks and strengthen data validation pipelines. Review and advise on country-level data analysis (Stata required; R a plus), ensuring analytical integrity, reproducibility, and appropriate interpretation of results. Quality-control MEL deliverables — including reports, dashboards, and presentations — and provide actionable feedback to raise the standard of country outputs. Help country MEL Leads translate data and evaluation findings into clear, decision-relevant insights for program teams and leadership. Actively identify and share learnings across your portfolio — bringing effective approaches from one country to another and flagging common challenges to the broader Global MEL team. Evaluation Design & Methodology Advise on evaluation design and review methodology across assigned programs, with fluency in quasi-experimental approaches (propensity score matching, difference-in-differences) and randomized controlled trials. Proactively identify methodological gaps or risks in ongoing evaluations and surface these to the relevant Global Senior Manager and MEL Director early — not just at reporting time. Contribute to the development and documentation of global MEL standards, evaluation frameworks, and shared analytical tools for use across country programs. Global MEL Initiatives Contribute to the design and rollout of MEL trainings and capacity-building programs for country MEL teams, translating global standards into practical, accessible learning materials. Support the development of shared tools, templates, and guidance documents that improve consistency and quality across One Acre Fund’s MEL portfolio. Contribute to cross-program methodology projects and special initiatives as prioritized by the Global MEL Director, which may include piloting new approaches, conducting portfolio-level analyses, or supporting strategic planning. Depending on candidate profile, provide dedicated analytical support to One Acre Fund’s Agroforestry portfolio. This is a large and technically complex program area with a range of open methodological questions; a key value of this support is having someone with the bandwidth to engage with these questions proactively throughout the year. Work would involve close collaboration with the Agroforestry team and MEL Director on measurement approaches, data systems, and building the evidence base for tree-related program outcomes. Peer review cross-country workstreams, providing quality control and suggesting areas for improvement. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have: We Are Seeking a Technically Strong MEL Professional With a Passion For Smallholder Agriculture And a Commitment To Evidence-based Program Improvement. Candidates Who Fit The Following Criteria Are Strongly Encouraged To Apply Analytical Excellence Advanced quantitative skills; proficiency in Stata is required. R is a strong plus. Demonstrated experience with impact evaluation design and methods, including propensity score matching (PSM), difference-in-differences (DiD), and/or randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Strong attention to detail and commitment to analytical rigor and reproducibility. Survey & Data Systems Experience designing and programming surveys for mobile data collection; CommCare experience is preferred. Demonstrated ability to design and improve data quality assurance processes, including back-check surveys and automated data validation. Experience & Education Minimum 3 years of professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, and/or applied research, preferably in international development. Master’s degree in economics, applied statistics, agricultural economics, or a closely related field. Experience working in Sub-Saharan Africa and with smallholder agricultural programs strongly preferred. Domain Knowledge Background in agriculture required; familiarity with common agricultural MEL frameworks and indicators (e.g., yield estimation, adoption surveys, income measurement) is a plus. Experience with agroforestry, tree planting programs, or forest ecosystem measurement is strongly preferred and will be a significant advantage in portfolio assignment. Communication & Collaboration Professional fluency in English required; strong written and verbal communication skills, including ability to translate complex findings for non-technical audiences. Professional fluency in French is a significant asset, particularly for candidates supporting DRC. Collaborative working style with a service orientation; comfortable providing structured feedback and coaching to peers and junior colleagues. Willingness to travel within the region (approximately 10–25% of time). Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Flexible, Countries of Operations Benefits Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits Contract Duration 2 Years Eligibility One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred. Application Deadline 04 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Vietnam represents a significant and underdeveloped market for women's economic opportunity. The country has a rapidly growing digital economy, a large and active informal MSME sector, and a financial system in transition — yet women-led enterprises and low-income women workers remain systematically underserved by formal finance. This role exists to change that. The Senior Principal will serve as WWB's primary representative in Vietnam: the lead advisor to financial services providers and partners, the lead voice with policy makers and regulators, and the lead relationship manager with funders and development finance institutions. Across all of these, the role carries genuine fundraising responsibility — this is not a delivery-only position but a business-building one. The role sits within the SEA regional team and carries a regional dimension: the Senior Principal will contribute meaningfully to programs in Indonesia, the Philippines, and Cambodia, bringing a cross-market perspective and supporting regional knowledge synthesis, product development, and advisory engagements as relevant. Vietnam, however, is the primary geographic mandate. The Senior Principal reports directly to the Regional Head of Southeast Asia and works in close coordination with the Advisory Director and Policy Director for technical guidance and quality assurance across their respective domains. The ideal candidate is commercially fluent, politically astute, and has deep roots in the Vietnamese financial sector — whether through banking, fintech, insurance, or development finance. They understand how to work inside institutions to drive change, how to translate evidence into funder commitments, and how to represent a global organization with credibility in local markets. Roles and Responsibilities Financial Service Provides Advisory Serve as WWB's primary in-country advisor to financial services providers — including banks, microfinance institutions, fintechs, and insurers — guiding the integration of gender-intelligent product design, alternative data-based underwriting, and women-centered customer experience. Drive the full advisory lifecycle — from business case development and diagnostic scoping through to implementation support, M&E, and knowledge documentation — with a focus on replicable, scalable models. Contribute to the design and execution of blended finance structures, first-loss facilities, and other financial instruments that de-risk FSP engagement with underserved women's segments. Represent WWB in regional and global knowledge-sharing with peer organizations, FSP networks, and research partners, integrating Vietnam evidence into cross-market learning. Policy Scoping and Regulatory Engagement Map and monitor Vietnam's regulatory landscape as it relates to financial inclusion, digital finance, microinsurance, MSME lending, and gender-responsive data — maintaining an active intelligence base that informs both program design and funder positioning. Build trusted relationships with the State Bank of Vietnam, Ministry of Finance, and other relevant authorities; identify strategic entry points for policy dialogue and position WWB as a credible, evidence-grounded voice. Track legislative and regulatory developments (including fintech licensing, open finance, credit registry reform, and climate finance) that may create or foreclose opportunity for women's financial inclusion. Produce high-quality policy briefs, regulatory analysis, and landscape reviews that support both internal strategy and external influence — in collaboration with regional research partners and WWB's global policy team. Liaise with multilateral institutions (ADB, IFC, World Bank, UN agencies), bilateral donors (DFAT, USAID, GIZ), and local civil society organizations active in Vietnam's inclusive finance ecosystem. Fundraising and Business Development Own and execute WWB's fundraising strategy for Vietnam — identifying, cultivating, and closing funding from foundations, bilateral donors, development finance institutions, corporate partners, and impact investors. Contribute to compelling funding proposals, concept notes, and investment cases that translate WWB's Vietnam programs into commercially and mission-aligned opportunities for funders. Contribute to existing funder relationships in-country, ensuring strong reporting, transparent communication, and proactive stewardship that supports grant renewals and relationship expansion. Contribute a robust pipeline of Vietnam-based funding opportunities, with clear ownership, timelines, and conversion targets; contribute to the regional pipeline as needed. Represent WWB at relevant funder convenings, industry conferences, and network events in Vietnam and regionally — building the organizational profile and personal credibility that attract inbound interest. Regional Contribution and Cross-Country Collaboration Participate actively as a member of the SEA regional team, contributing to program design, knowledge synthesis, and advisory engagements in Indonesia, the Philippines, and Cambodia — particularly on areas of Vietnamese-market relevance (e.g., supply chain finance, climate-health risk, factory worker segments). Contribute Vietnam-sourced evidence, case studies, and learning to regional research agendas and cross-market analytical products. Support the Regional Director and regional team with regional strategy development, funder presentations, board materials, and partner engagement as required. Help build WWB's institutional knowledge on operating in Vietnam — legal, regulatory, and partnership infrastructure. Required Qualifications Skills & Attributes Commercially fluent and commercially ambitious — able to articulate the market case for women's financial inclusion in language that resonates with FSPs, investors, and development finance institutions, not just development sector audiences. Entrepreneurial and self-directed, with a demonstrated capacity to build programs and partnerships from the ground up in ambiguous or resource-constrained environments. Policy-literate and regulatory-savvy — comfortable engaging with government counterparts, interpreting regulatory developments, and translating policy context into program implications. Evidence-grounded — values data, is rigorous about claims, and uses research and proof points to build credibility with skeptical stakeholders. Strong writer and communicator, with the ability to tailor voice and framing for multiple audiences: FSP leadership, government officials, funders, and internal team. Highly collaborative — able to work effectively across a dispersed regional team, contribute to shared workstreams, and operate without a local team around them. Culturally intelligent and locally rooted — understands the Vietnamese business culture, relationship norms, and institutional landscape, and can represent a global organization with authenticity in-country. Comfortable with complexity and ambiguity — able to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously and make sound judgments in dynamic, fast-paced environments. Minimum 12 years of professional experience across financial services, development finance, financial inclusion, or related fields — with a significant portion of that experience in Vietnam. Demonstrated track record in fundraising or business development — including proposal writing, funder relationship management, and grant or contract conversion. Substantial experience in FSP advisory, product development, or financial sector consulting — including direct engagement with FSP leadership and boards. Experience engaging with government and regulatory stakeholders in Vietnam; existing relationships with SBV, MOF, or relevant authorities strongly preferred. Strong analytical and writing skills; ability to produce high-quality documents (proposals, briefs, program reports) independently and under time pressure. Demonstrated ability to work independently and as part of a remote, geographically distributed team. Fluency in Vietnamese and English (written and spoken) — both are required. Willingness to travel within Vietnam and regionally across the SEA footprint (Indonesia, Philippines, Cambodia) as required. Preferred Qualifications Prior experience with international NGOs, impact investment vehicles, or bilateral/multilateral development programs in Vietnam. Familiarity with blended finance structures, de-risking facilities, or development finance instruments (IFC, ADB, DFI-type engagements). Experience with gender-lens investing, women's economic empowerment programming, or financial inclusion for low-income segments. Networks within Vietnam's fintech, digital finance, or insurance sectors.
